title: Symplectic form is unchanged by restricting the second argument
statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and an integer $n$, and work in the space $V = \bbf_p^{\,n} \times \bbf_p^{\,n}$ equipped with the symplectic form $\omega$. Let $M \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ be a set of coordinates, and let $v \in V_M$, so that every coordinate of $v$ lying outside $M$ vanishes. Then for every $s \in V$,
\[
\omega(v, s) = \omega(v, r_M(s)),
\]
where $r_M(s)$ is the vector obtained from $s$ by zeroing out all coordinates outside $M$.
hypotheses_covered: M is a subset of the coordinate index set Fin n
v lies in the support submodule V_M (v vanishes outside M)
s is an arbitrary vector of V
replaced: If $v \in V_M$, then $\omega(v,s) = \omega(v, r_M(s))$ for all $s \in V$.
